summary:
Secrets of Breathing Gaia is an interactive, brutalist aerospace-themed web application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. 

What we developed: 
An immersive dashboard powered by React, TypeScript, and Three.js featuring a 3D interactive globe with custom data nodes across global sectors. It includes isolated data channels ("Earth's Secrets," "Ocean Explorer," "Endangered Species," "Planet in Motion," and "Satellite Fleet"), multimedia modals, and an AI trivia terminal ("Gaia Oracle").

How it addresses the challenge: 
The platform transforms complex open-source Earth observation data and research-backed regional insights into an intuitive information jukebox. Users can lock the globe onto specific continental sectors, filter data strictly by environmental channel, and inspect localized ecological intel—such as Himalayan terrain mechanics and endangered species telemetry.

Why it is important: 
Translating dense satellite telemetry into engaging public tools is vital for environmental education and climate action. By bridging complex geospatial data with an accessible, gamified digital archive, our project inspires planetary stewardship and highlights the critical importance of global environmental monitoring.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

• Secrets of Breathing Gaia is an interactive, brutalist aerospace-themed web application that operates as an "Earth Information Jukebox"[cite: 15].

• It merges a 3D interactive globe (built with Three.js and globe.gl) with a centralized database of 30 curated regional nodes across all continents.

• Users select a continental sector to lock the camera view and choose from isolated channels ("Earth's Secrets," "Ocean Explorer," "Endangered Species," "Planet in Motion," and "Satellite Fleet")[cite: 15].

• Clicking a globe marker triggers a sci-fi "Space HUD" tactical modal displaying localized research, natural calamities, NASA telemetry data, embedded video media (such as custom field edits for the Himalayas), and targeted ecological intelligence[cite: 15].

• It also includes an AI trivia terminal ("Gaia Oracle") with an interactive "Fact or Myth" challenge mode[cite: 15].

What benefits does it have?

• High-Density, Clutter-Free Data Isolation: Unlike traditional dashboards that overwhelm users with all data points simultaneously, our layer-management system strictly filters data by channel, eliminating cross-contamination between topics like wildlife tracking and tectonic hazards[cite: 15].

• Immersive Engagement: Combines educational scientific rigor with a gamified trivia challenge and ambient synth audio to maintain high user engagement[cite: 15].

• Accessible and Public-Ready: Functions as a responsive web application that runs smoothly locally and deploys instantly for public access without requiring external logins or heavy software installations[cite: 4, 7, 15].

What is the intended impact of the project?

• Democratizing Earth Science: Translating complex open-source satellite data and dense scientific literature into an intuitive, visually striking format makes planetary health understandable for students, educators, and the general public[cite: 15].

• Inspiring Environmental Stewardship: By highlighting regional vulnerabilities—such as glacial retreat, mangrove loss, and endangered habitats—the project fosters a deeper emotional connection to Earth's ecosystems and encourages proactive climate awareness[cite: 15].

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

• Coding Languages & Frameworks: React, TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3[cite: 15].

• Libraries & Visualization: Three.js and globe.gl for 3D geospatial rendering; Lucide React for aerospace-grade UI iconography[cite: 15].

• Data Sources & Media: Custom research-backed regional datasets, NASA open telemetry APIs (EONET v3), and custom short-form video media[cite: 15].

• Development Environment: Visual Studio Code, Git/GitHub for version control, and Node.js (npm run dev) for local environment testing[cite: 15].

How is your project creative?

• Thematic Consistency: Conceptualized as an "aerospace terminal" featuring typewriter title animations, glassmorphism, coordinate tracking chips, and a dynamic cosmic starfield with drifting stars and shooting meteors rather than a standard corporate design[cite: 15].

• The "Jukebox" Metaphor: Treating global telemetry like music tracks to be "tuned into" transforms dry scientific monitoring into an artistic, interactive experience[cite: 15].

• Dynamic Multi-Layer Modals: The system dynamically re-renders modal content based on the active channel, offering a tailored storytelling experience for every click[cite: 15].

What factors did your team consider?

• User Experience & Scannability: Balanced heavy scientific text with clean spacing, high-contrast visual accents (muted olive greens, electric blues, and soft peach highlights), and custom scrollbars to prevent layout fatigue[cite: 15].

• Performance & Responsiveness: Ensured the 3D WebGL globe runs fluidly across browsers while handling spatial coordinate filtering and audio synthesis without lag[cite: 15].

• Hackathon Constraints: Designed a modular codebase that is easy to deploy, robust against network errors via built-in fallbacks, and fully optimized for judging criteria including impact, creativity, validity, and presentation[cite: 10, 15].
